title: [CQ-R11c] Host check session and outcome
description:
Objective: the host runs one check in a guest through `multipass exec ... moe-supervisor check`. It sends the approved check frame first and classifies how the check ended into the daemon's CheckOutcome values, with a bounded output tail. It never yields 'passed' without a clean observation.

Split from CQ-R11 (task-0795112597cb453f93aaa5106e92d023) on 2026-10-29. It depends on:
- CQ-R10c (task-3b70b824), because both edit guest-bridge.mjs;
- CQ-R11b (task-9048e7ec), for the supervisor check mode and its exit codes, which the end-to-end test drives.

Contract:
- scripts/local-runner/guest-bridge.mjs:
  - checkArgv(name) = ['exec', '--no-map-working-directory', name, '--', 'sudo', '-n', GUEST_LAYOUT.supervisor, 'check'], frozen, for owned instance names only;
  - checkFrame({id, command, protected}) returns the exact CQ-R11a frame bytes. It applies the same id, command and protected rules and refuses with a fixed BRIDGE_* code.
- A new scripts/local-runner/check-session.mjs: runCheckSession({name, check, provider, budgetMs, timeoutMs, signal}).
  - It validates every input before spawn, then spawns checkArgv and writes the check frame as the first stdin bytes.
  - It accepts only hello, output and exactly one observation. A request frame ends the session, because a check job has no Moe route. Reuse guest-bridge's decoder and parseGuestFrame.
  - It keeps at most the last 16384 UTF-8 bytes of combined output, cut on a character boundary (CheckRun.outputTail's rule).
  - budgetMs is the host's wall-clock budget. When it fires, the session closes stdin (the supervisor kills and reaps the group), then kills the local provider after timeoutMs.
  - It resolves a frozen {outcome, exitCode, signal, outputTail}, where outcome is:
    - 'passed': observation code 0 and supervisor exit 0;
    - 'code-failure': a nonzero code or a signal;
    - 'inconclusive': CQ-R11b's post-run protected-change code;
    - 'skipped': CQ-R11b's pre-run protected mismatch;
    - 'timeout': the budget fired;
    - 'infra-failure': spawn, protocol, provider or other supervisor failures.
  - A local kill is never evidence that the guest job ended.
- Tests in scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs: fake-provider rows for every outcome and refusal, and an end-to-end row through the real supervisor's check mode with injected Python seams (python3 -I -B).

Out of scope: VM lifecycle and deletion (CQ-R11), environment identity (CQ-R11d), the daemon's ingestion (CQ-V03), dispatch (CQ-V04), and any verified-local or isolation claim.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs (on WSL: env -i with the nvm Node 24 PATH).
definitionOfDone: The check frame is the first stdin write and byte-exact, invalid check input refuses before spawn with a fixed code, and checkArgv is fixed and accepts owned names only. Shown by tests.

Each outcome (passed, code-failure, inconclusive, skipped, timeout, infra-failure) arises only from its condition, and a request frame, a missing observation or a nonzero supervisor exit never yields passed. Shown by tests.
outputTail keeps at most the last 16384 UTF-8 bytes, starting on a whole character. Shown by tests.
An end-to-end test runs the real supervisor's check mode and gets 'passed' and 'code-failure' from real exit codes. The verification command exits 0, and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
checkArgv and checkFrame in scripts/local-runner/guest-bridge.mjs, plus rows C1-C2 in scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs (DoD 1).

Read first: the LANDED R10c bytes of guest-bridge.mjs (AGENT_JOBS, jobFrame, and exactKeys as a key-set comparison) and the LANDED R11a/R11b supervisor (read_check's rules and the constants PROTECTED_MISMATCH = 79 and PROTECTED_CHANGED = 80). This plan follows their approved plans; if the landed code differs, follow it and note it.

guest-bridge.mjs:
- checkArgv(name): owned names only (isOwnedInstanceName), else BRIDGE_INPUT_INVALID. Return Object.freeze(['exec', '--no-map-working-directory', name, '--', 'sudo', '-n', GUEST_LAYOUT.supervisor, 'check']), exactly like bridgeArgv.
- checkFrame({id, command, protected}) returns encodeFrame({kind: 'check', version: 1, id, command, protected}), built from validated copies in that key order. Any refusal throws bridgeError('BRIDGE_INPUT_INVALID'). The rules mirror the supervisor's read_check, which mirrors the daemon:
  - input: a plain record whose key set is exactly {id, command, protected} (R10c's exactKeys);
  - id: /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$/;
  - command: a string with command.trim() !== '', command.isWellFormed(), length <= 1000 (String.length is UTF-16 units, as the supervisor measures) and no /[\u0000-\u001f\u007f-\u009f  ]/;
  - protected: an array of at most 2000 entries, each a plain record whose keys are exactly {path, oid}:
    - oid matches /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/;
    - path is a well-formed string of at most 500 units, with no '\\', '�' or control character, and no '' / '.' / '..' segment;
    - paths are strictly ascending by Buffer.compare of their UTF-8.
  Copy the entries as {path, oid} literals, so a later caller edit or a getter cannot change the bytes.
- Error handling: fixed text only (bridgeError); no value is ever echoed.

Tests (CQ-R11c section):
- C1:
  - checkArgv: deepEqual to the literal for an owned name, and Object.isFrozen. 'vm', '', 'moe-x', 42 and undefined each give BRIDGE_INPUT_INVALID.
  - checkFrame: for a valid input, the bytes equal a 4-byte big-endian length + JSON.stringify of the literal frame, built in the test. Each refusal class gives BRIDGE_INPUT_INVALID with the fixed message: bad and boundary ids, commands and paths, an extra or missing key, unsorted or duplicate paths, 2001 entries, a lone '\ud800' in a command or path, and non-record input.
- C2, drift; skip on win32 (POSIX python3):
  - Table-drive about 16 boundary inputs through BOTH sides: 64/65-char ids; 1000/1001 commands; '\x9f' vs '\xa0'; ' '; 500/501-unit paths; 2000/2001 entries; '.', '..', '' and '\\' paths.
  - The supervisor side runs read_check through R11a's python3 -I -B importlib loader on a pipe holding the frame. Host-refused inputs are framed by hand with the same JSON. Assert that checkFrame accepts exactly when read_check returns, and refuses exactly when read_check raises ValueError.
  - Also assert that the supervisor's m.PROTECTED_MISMATCH and m.PROTECTED_CHANGED equal check-session.mjs's constants (step 2 exports them).

End-to-end row C7 through the real supervisor's check mode (DoD 4).

Skip on win32 (POSIX python3), and with R11a K3's busy-host RLIMIT_NPROC guard, since GUARD forks the job as the test user.

- provider.spawn ignores multipass's argv except its final 'check' (assert it), and runs spawnProcess('python3', ['-I', '-B', '-c', LOAD + harness, SUPERVISOR, workspace, sessions], {stdio: 'pipe'}).
- The harness:
  - stubs m.protect_mounts with a no-op;
  - calls sys.exit(m.main(['check'], geteuid=lambda: 0, workspace=, sessions=, identity=(os.getuid(), os.getgid(), None), netns=False)).
  stdin is the session's own pipe, so the check frame really travels as the first write.
- Rows. Commands are shell builtins only, so the job forks nothing:
  - 'exit 0' resolves {outcome: 'passed', exitCode: 0, signal: null, outputTail: ''};
  - 'echo boom; exit 3' resolves 'code-failure', exitCode 3, outputTail 'boom\n';
  - a protected entry with a flipped oid resolves 'skipped' from the real exit 79, with no job.
- Kill your own leftovers in after(): spawnSync timeouts and pgrep markers, per gotcha-local-runner-supervisor-tests.

Error handling: a harness failure must fail the row, never skip it.

Verification. Run this once, fresh, from the repo root: `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs`.

On WSL, run `env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs`. Exit 0 is required, and its output tail is the complete_task verification evidence (DoD 4).

Also confirm the following. They are not evidence.
- Every pre-existing bridge (B, S, I, H, J) and check (E, K) row passes unchanged, with no removed line in either test file.
- No scripts/local-runner/__pycache__.
- git diff --numstat plus wc -l of the new module totals at most 400 changed lines. Budget: runtime up to 160 (bridge about 35, session about 125) and tests up to 240.
  If the honest diff exceeds 400, do not cut a DoD row. Stop, and comment on the task with the measured split, so the architect can propose a size rail as for R08/R09c.
- LF line endings.

Note peers' dirty paths and continue. Error handling for the gate itself: fix a failure's cause with a test, never by weakening or skipping a row, then re-run the whole command.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Rejected these options:
1) Extending runGuestSession with a check mode. It would entangle forwarding and pending-request logic with a session that must refuse requests, and edit R08/R10c's file. A separate, smaller module mirrors its proven structure instead.
2) A hello deadline. Pre-run work (re-own, blob hashing, mounts) happens before hello, and budgetMs already bounds everything.
3) Keeping only the last 16384 raw bytes. U+FFFD expansion and a partial first sequence could leak into the kept end, so keep a 32 KiB raw window and cut after normalizing.
4) Rejecting on abort. The contract resolves an outcome after validation; only input refusal throws.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- guest-session.mjs (R08) is the template: input validation, child shape check, later/cancel, a stop that destroys stdin then SIGKILLs the provider after timeoutMs, and a settle that runs once.
- The bridge tests' fakeProvider (local-runner-bridge.test.mjs:618) exits 74 on stdin close and closes asynchronously on kill.
- parseGuestFrame validates exact guest kinds and returns output data as bytes. The observation shape is {kind, type: 'exit', code|null, signal|null}.
- ASSUMED from approved, unlanded plans:
  - R10c: AGENT_JOBS/jobFrame, exactKeys as a key set;
  - R11a: read_check, main(['check']) with seams workspace/sessions/identity/netns, LOAD harness;
  - R11b: PROTECTED_MISMATCH 79 pre-hello, PROTECTED_CHANGED 80 after the observation, m.protect_mounts.
- The daemon's CheckRun tail rule is checkRunStore.ts (MAX_CHECK_LOG_BYTES 16384, then skip continuation bytes).
planningNotes.risks:
- Size: 400 is tight. The budget is in step 5, and the fallback is a size-rail proposal, never cutting DoD rows.
- C7 depends on three unlanded slices. Adapt to the landed names, and keep the outcome rules.
- Fake-provider masking:
  - a synchronous close masks the kill path;
  - a fake whose stdin close doesn't exit masks the budget path; use hung only where intended.
- C7 is RLIMIT_NPROC-sensitive on busy hosts; use R11a K3's guard.
- String.prototype.isWellFormed needs Node 20+. CI uses Node 24 and WSL uses the nvm Node 24.
